subject: ApexAI renewal: capacity rechannel & throttling policy for hosted commit uplift
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Lin <maya@apexai.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + ask: bump monthly commit and consolidate rate bands

Hi Stephanie / Aditya,

Hope you’re both well. We’re approaching renewal for our hosted API plan (current commit: 2.5M tokens/month) and seeing consistent growth from two new feature launches. The team is forecasting ~4–5M tokens/month by August and wants to simplify tiering — specifically:

- Move to a single higher monthly commit with a tighter set of rate bands (fewer breakpoints) to reduce billing surprises for product teams.
- Increase burst capacity during weekend ML training windows but apply a throttling policy to avoid noisy traffic spikes affecting latency SLOs.

Can Redwood propose a path to upgrade commit with a short-term trial for the burst uplift (30 days) and a recommended throttle (per-second or per-user limits) we can enforce on our side? Also please include the usage export for Q1 so procurement has detailed numbers.

Maya will loop in procurement if we have a clear proposal. Looking to lock terms in May.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Product, ApexAI
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + ask: bump monthly commit and consolidate rate bands

Thanks Sanjay — this is useful context.

Short answer: yes, we can do a staged commit uplift plus a 30-day burst window with a controlled throttling policy. I’ll ask Ben to run a costed proposal with two pathways: a standard uplift (12-month amendment) and a pilot path (60-day pilot + then annual commit).

Requests from our side to size the options:
- Q1 export: total tokens by route (ingest vs. generate) and median vs. 95th pct latency windows.
- Preferred billing cadence and whether you need a single consolidated invoice across business units.

Ben — can you prepare a numbers-first proposal and include an ops play for throttling (suggested per-user TPS limits, backoff guidance, and canary rollout steps)? I’ve attached the initial SOW template we use for amendments (see drive link).

-Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com>, Maya Lin <maya@apexai.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: two-path uplift + throttle policy (proposal attached)

Hi all — attaching the proposal and an uplift worksheet: Redwood_Uplift_Proposal_ApexAI_v2.xlsx and a short ops note (draft_amendment_rechannel_throttle_policy.pdf). Highlights:

1) Two pathways
  a) Pilot: temporary +50% commit (effective for 30 days) with a one-time pilot fee; if usage stabilizes, convert to an annual commit at a 10% uplift over current price.
  b) Straight renewal: upgrade to a new 12-month commit at 4.5M tokens/mo with consolidated rate bands (3 bands instead of 7) and a 7% volume discount applied.

2) Throttle policy (ops):
  - Default per-token QPS limit: 450 RPS per region; per-user soft limit of 40 RPS (helps noisy endpoints).
  - Weekend burst window: allow additional 1.5x burst capacity for scheduled training jobs; bursts must be registered with Redwood 48 hours in advance.
  - Canary: route 5% of calls to the higher capacity pool for 48 hours before full rollout.

3) Billing and PO path: we can accept PO for the pilot, with invoice net-30 for production commits.

Attachments: proposal worksheet, usage assumptions, and sample amendment. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/1749

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Uplift_Proposal_ApexAI_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), draft_amendment_rechannel_throttle_policy.pdf (pdf), ApexAI_MAAP_usage_report_Q1.pdf (csv export -> pdf)
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Lin <maya@apexai.com>, Procurement <procurement@apexai.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: two-path uplift + throttle policy (proposal attached)

Thanks Ben — reviewed the worksheet. A few procurement/ops items before we can proceed:

- Can you tighten the billing tiers so we have a clearer per-token marginal price above commit? Right now the consolidated bands look cleaner but procurement wants predictable marginal rates for forecasting.
- For the weekend burst: can we instead implement a token-based burst budget (e.g., 500k tokens per weekend) tied to registered runs? Easier for us to track internally.
- Our security team also wants to confirm that the canary routing will not send PII to any non-primary region — we need assurances about region pinning during the 5% canary.

If those are OK, procurement will issue a PO for the pilot. Can we also get an editable amendment to drop into our contract system?

-Sanjay
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: two-path uplift + throttle policy (proposal attached)

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 10:22 AM Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — reviewed the worksheet. A few procurement/ops items before we can proceed:
>
> - Can you tighten the billing tiers so we have a clearer per-token marginal price above commit?
> - For the weekend burst: can we instead implement a token-based burst budget (e.g., 500k tokens per weekend) tied to registered runs?
> - Our security team also wants to confirm that the canary routing will not send PII to any non-primary region — we need assurances about region pinning during the 5% canary.

Great questions — quick answers inline: 

- Billing tiers: yes — Ben will add marginal per-token lines for each consolidated band so forecasting is explicit. We can also include an example invoice row in the amendment.
- Weekend burst as token budget: we can implement token-bucket style bursts (preferred) and expose the registered-run API so you can reserve weekend budget. We’ll add a 2nd column to the proposal that shows cost impact for 250k / 500k / 1M weekend budgets.
- Canary region pinning: confirmed. Canary traffic will honor your region pinning and will not cross regions; we’ll set explicit routing rules in the amendment and a pre-roll checklist for security.

I’m attaching an editable amendment draft (draft_amendment_rechannel_throttle_policy.pdf) — Ben, can you create an editable .docx and a version with the marginal price table?

Next steps: Ben to update the worksheet + marginal pricing by EOD Fri. Sanjay / Procurement to confirm if a pilot PO will be issued for the 30-day test. If yes, Ops will schedule the weekend burst registration flow and security checklist.

Thanks — Steph
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apexai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@apexai.com>, Maya Lin <maya@apexai.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: two-path uplift + throttle policy (proposal attached)

Steph / Ben — procurement has approved the pilot PO (attached: signed_intent_apexai.pdf). We reviewed the updated worksheet and the marginal pricing table looks good. We’ll start with the 500k token weekend budget for the pilot and register the first weekend run for May 2–3.

We still need the editable amendment for legal, but procurement has cleared the PO path for the pilot. Please send the DocuSign when the amendment is ready and confirm the canary routing config so our security team can sign off.

Appreciate the responsiveness — excited to get the uplift into production.

Best,
Sanjay
